newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen riding up on dollar, rates.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen riding up on dollar, rates.

text.p: The strong dollar and easing long term interest rates helped the Brussels bourse set new intra-day and closing record highs on Tuesday, and traders said there was more in store.
"The dollar remains strong and long term interest rates are back below six percent. There is no bad news for the moment. That is the reason the market is strong," one trader said.

The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended an active day up 11.46 points or 0.50 percent at a new closing high of 2,280.77, having at one stage hit a new intra-day high of 2,289.88. Nearly four billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.
Star performer of the day was oil major PetroFina which ended unchanged at 12,450 francs in a volume of more than 55,000 shares as a share buying warrant expired.

Traders said that although the warrant was to buy shares at 12,500 francs -- above the market price -- the fee structure for professionals meant they could effectively obtain the shares at around 12,410 francs.

They had then been feeding them onto the market at around 12,475 -- the price the share kept fluctuating up to during the day. Traders said it was too early to say how many warrants had been exercised and therefore how much capital PetroFina had got.
Elsewhere it was the dollar sensitives which rode the crest of the Brussels wave.
Kredietbank was up 2.1 percent to 14,900 francs, steel cord and wire maker Bekaert climbed 1.8 percent to 21,500 francs and non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere was up 1.5 percent to 2,965.
Banque Bruxelles Lambert was up one percent to 9,820 francs, retailer Delhaize was up 0.8 percent to 1,820 francs and Generale Bank was 0.7 percent higher at 14,075 francs.

Traders said the worries over the future of the European Union's single currency project caused by the victory of Left wing parties in the French elections had lifted the dollar and would continue to support it.
"There are suddenly lots of uncertainties again," one trader said.

"It will be a political decision, and the political will is still there. But we will have to wait until the Amsterdam summit (on June 16 and 17) to see what becomes of the Stability Pact and the (Maastricht Treaty) criteria," he added.
